summary: Macro backdrop for ags: headwind (score -6 across rates, dollar, Brazil real, risk, energy, China, breadth). rates 0; dollar −; brl −; risk −; energy −; china −; breadth −. Strongest ag/soft over the month: Rough rice +4.5%; weakest: Lean hogs -15.3%. Key releases ahead: US Core PCE Price Index m/m (11-25 8:30 AM ET); US Prelim GDP q/q (11-25 8:30 AM ET).

sections.title: Rates
sections.text: US 10-year 4.92% (-8 bp in a month), 2-year 4.63% (-6 bp); 2s10s curve +29 bp (-2 bp in a month). Yields are little changed on the month. T-bill yield 4.15% sets the cost of carrying inventory.

sections.title: Dollar & farm currencies
sections.text: Dollar index 104.33 (+2.5% in a month, +6.2% YTD). A stronger dollar makes US grain, oilseeds, cotton and meat dearer abroad. USD/BRL 5.930 (+17.4% in a month): a weaker real encourages Brazilian farmer selling of soybeans, corn, sugar, coffee and cotton, pressuring world prices. USD/CNY 6.664 (-0.2%); USD/MXN 19.15 (+2.3%).

sections.title: Risk appetite
sections.text: S&P 500 -5.1% in a month (+5.7% YTD); VIX 26.6. Risk-off: funds tend to cut commodity length along with equities.

sections.title: Energy
sections.text: WTI 80.44 $/bbl (-20.3% in a month), Brent 86.87, ULSD 3.656 $/gal (-21.8%), natural gas 3.54 (+0.9%). Lower crude weighs on soybean oil and corn through biofuel margins and on cotton via cheaper polyester.

sections.title: China & industrial demand
sections.text: Copper -13.8% in a month, Shanghai Composite -4.1%, Hang Seng -3.1%, yuan +0.2% vs USD. Soft China/industrial signals point to weaker import demand.

sections.title: Commodity breadth
sections.text: 7 of 33 commodities trade above their 50-day average (21%); S&P GSCI -15.4% in a month; gold -9.4%.

caveat: Directional channels from macro to ag prices are standard relationships, not signals tested on this desk; use as context.
